card.name: Otea
card.tagline: Fast hip-shaking Tahitian group dance to drums.
card.profile: The oteea is a percussion-driven group dance with rapid hip motion, danced in several rows. Once a male warrior dance, it now has male (oteea tane), female (oteea vahine) and mixed (oteea amui) forms. Dancers execute figures (tamau, varu, otamu, ami, faarapu) while gesturing daily-life, nature or warfare themes. Accompaniment is drums only - the toere slit-log drum, the sharkskin pahu, and the smaller faatete - with no singing. Costumes use long plant-fiber (more) skirts with tassels and elaborate headpieces (English Wikipedia; Air Tahiti Nui).
card.insight: Considered Tahiti's most spectacular dance; its modern choreography was standardized when Madeleine Moua founded the Heiva troupe in 1956 (English Wikipedia).
